The Story of Nebraska Furniture Mart Intelligent Investment Today - The Warren Buffett Way 20m Why did Warren Buffett buy Nebraska Furniture Mart , and what made Rose Blumkin (Mrs. B) one of the greatest entrepreneurs he ever encountered?

 In this episode of Intelligent Investment Today , David Coombs explores one of Warren Buffett's most fascinating acquisitions and uncovers the timeless investing lessons hidden inside an apparently ordinary furniture retailer.

 Starting with just $500 and unable to speak English, Rose Blumkin built Nebraska Furniture Mart into one of America's most successful retail businesses through a simple philosophy: "Sell cheap and tell the truth." Buffett recognised far more than a successful retailer—he saw exceptional management, a powerful competitive advantage, outstanding business economics and a company built around genuine customer value.

 You'll discover:

  Why Warren Buffett invested in Nebraska Furniture Mart   The remarkable story of entrepreneur Rose Blumkin (Mrs. B)   How low prices became a lasting competitive advantage   The importance of business moats, scale and operational efficiency   Why Buffett thinks like a business owner—not a stock market trader   Practical value investing lessons every long-term investor can apply  Whether you're interested in value investing , Warren Buffett , Benjamin Graham , Berkshire Hathaway , or identifying high-quality businesses with durable competitive advantages, this episode offers practical insights into how intelligent investors evaluate companies beyond the daily movements of the stock market.

 If you enjoy long-term investing, business analysis and learning from the world's greatest investors, subscribe to Intelligent Investment Today for weekly episodes exploring the principles behind successful investing.
